title: compat: implicit-tool-params-and-choice-rank-encoding-for-openai-invoke
author: Sofia Ramirez
description:
Motivation: OpenAI-style function/tool calling clients commonly omit explicit parameter fields when invoking tools (they rely on positional/implicit context or merge params into the message body). The compatibility layer previously required a near-exact schema mapping which caused failures when: 1) clients sent tool params inline in the assistant message, 2) tool_choice events arrived without an explicit schema reference, or 3) streaming fragments split an initial tool message header from its json payload.

Summary: This PR relaxes and documents the OpenAI compatibility layer's handling of implicit tool parameters and introduces a stable, compact "choice rank" encoding for tool_choice events to make tiebreak and telemetry deterministic across retries and streaming fragment reassembly.

Key changes:
- compat/invoke_mapper: add ImplicitParamResolver that inspects assistant/tool messages and maps inline params to the canonical tool call payload (applies heuristics for common patterns, configurable per-route).
- compat/choice: replace ad-hoc choice string with a 2-field encoded metadata (rank:int + reason:str) to preserve deterministic ordering when multiple tools are equally scored; exposes the raw reason to telemetry but keeps the public wire format compact.
- streaming/fragmenter: improve fragment boundary detection to avoid splitting a tool payload across frames when the payload is small and fits remaining buffer; add a reassembly path that tags fragments with the choice rank metadata to prevent double-invoke races.
- telemetry: add event.choice_resolve_reason and event.choice_rank to tooling traces and request-level traces so we can audit tiebreak decisions.
- docs: update openai-compat/README with examples of implicit param patterns and migration notes.
- tests: new unit + integration tests for fragmented tool payloads, implicit param mapping heuristics, and choice rank determinism.

Design notes and constraints:
- Heuristics are intentionally conservative: we only auto-map inline params when the assistant message contains an explicit "invoke" marker or syntactic patterns (JSON-like blocks, key:value lines) and when the target tool signature is compatible. There is a per-route flag (compat.allow_implicit_tool_params) defaulting to false for safety; the hosted default for well-known OpenAI endpoints flips it on.
- Choice rank encoding: we use a short base36-encoded string for the wire form (example: "r3-xF" where r3 is rank 3 and xF is hashed reason fragment) to keep streaming overhead minimal while preserving determinism.
- Backwards compatibility: old clients still accepted; when choice metadata is missing we fallback to previous stable tie heuristics but emit a telemetry warning.

Testing & CI:
- Added 6 unit test files and 2 integration tests that run against the streaming harness (perf impact measured: negligible serialization CPU delta in smoke tests).
- CI: lint, unit, integration (streaming harness) all pass; flaky streaming test was hardened.

Rollout plan:
- Feature gated behind compat.allow_implicit_tool_params and a small percentage rollout for the new choice rank telemetry.
- Monitor event.choice_resolve_reason and event.choice_rank distribution; run alert if >0.1% of requests hit the fallback path.

Migration notes for customers:
- No action required for most customers. If you rely on exact tool-call payload ordering or custom proxies that mutate assistant messages, consider enabling additional logging and/or the new per-route safety flag until you validate.

Related work: ENG-1472 (openai invoke reliability), ENG-1499 (streaming fragment reassembly).

review_comments: Kenji Tanaka (2026-02-19): Left a couple of suggestions on the implicit mapping heuristics. Are we able to make the per-route flag dynamic so SRE can toggle quickly without restarts?
Sofia Ramirez (2026-02-19): Reply: added a dynamic flag path that reads from config store on change; documented in routes/default_config.yaml. SRE can toggle via console.
Priya Shah (2026-02-22): Can we add an explicit unit test showing a three-way tie where choice_rank makes the decision deterministic across retries? The current tests show two-way ties only.
Sofia Ramirez (2026-02-23): Added test for three-way tie (tests/compat/test_three_way_choice_rank.py), included in CI.
Liam O'Connor (2026-02-26): Fragment reassembly looks good but we should ensure we never buffer unboundedly waiting for missing fragments. Suggest a 250ms reassembly timeout by default.
Sofia Ramirez (2026-02-26): Added reassembly timeout and metrics for reassembly_timeouts. Default 250ms, configurable via streaming.reassembly_timeout_ms.
release_notes: OpenAI compat: support for implicit tool parameter mapping (opt-in per-route), deterministic choice_rank wire encoding for tool_choice events (improves retries and streaming reassembly). Added telemetry for choice resolution. No breaking changes by default; feature gated.
notes_for_ops: Monitor telemetry.event.choice_resolve_reason and telemetry.event.choice_rank; watch reassembly_timeouts metric. If spike in fallback path, revert rollout and open ENG-1472 followup.
